name: AI Bot Crawlability
description: Parses the origin's robots.txt and tests, for each of the 126 AI crawler user-agent tokens in the bundled ai-robots-txt list, whether that bot may crawl the current page path. If AI crawlers are blocked they cannot fetch the page, so it cannot be cited or used by AI search and assistants.

scoring.summary: Site check at path /. No robots.txt: 8/12 (inconclusive when it is generated at build time). Empty robots.txt: 12. Otherwise each bot in references/ai-bots.json is tested with the RFC 9309 parser. The 10 major bots share 9 points and the other 116 share 3; blocking any major bot caps the score at 9; any allowed bot with Crawl-delay over 5s costs 2. Status follows the shared 80% / 50% rule.

rules.condition: no robots.txt in the served root and no robots.txt generator
rules.message: robots.txt not found - all bots allowed by default

rules.condition: Generated robots.txt (no file in the served root, but src/pages/robots.txt.*, app/robots.*, robots.njk/robots.11ty.js, Hugo enableRobotsTXT, astro-robots-txt / next-sitemap, or a CMS in report-only mode)
robots.txt body is empty after trim()

parser (lib/robots.mjs, RFC 9309): '#' comments stripped; consecutive User-agent lines form one group sharing its rules; user-agent tokens match case-insensitively; a bot with its own group ignores the * group
path match: the longest matching Allow/Disallow pattern wins, Allow wins a tie; '*' matches any sequence, trailing '$' anchors; empty Disallow ignored; path tested is '/'
crawl delay: the largest Crawl-delay among the groups that apply to the bot (no inheritance of the * delay by bots with their own group); only counted for allowed bots

rules.points: Math.round(9 * majorAllowed / 10 + 3 * otherAllowed / 116), where the 10 major bots are listed in references/ai-bots.json (major_bots)

rules.condition: one or more allowed bots have crawl-delay > 5

rules.note: one finding per blocking robots.txt rule (file + line, first 5 bots named) and one per Crawl-delay group over 5s

bot_list.source: src/data/robots.json (ai-robots-txt/ai.robots.txt), keys of the top-level object, loaded via utils.loadBotList() and cached in chrome.storage.local under botListVersion '1.0.0'
bot_list.prioritized: none - every bot has equal weight in allowedCount/totalBots

scoring.status_mapping: Derived by the engine from the integer score: >= 80% pass, >= 50% warning, else fail; inconclusive results are always a warning.
scoring.inconclusive: Only when robots.txt is generated (endpoint, framework route, plugin, CMS virtual file) and not present in the served root: 8/12 with inconclusive true. An absent robots.txt in the served root is an informative absence (it will 404 on a static host).

detect.source_procedure: 1) Read robots.txt from the served root (build output, else the source public dir, else the repo root). 2) If absent: if a generator exists (src/pages/robots.txt.*, app/robots.*, robots.njk, robots.11ty.js, Hugo enableRobotsTXT, astro-robots-txt / next-sitemap, CMS) report 8 inconclusive, else 8 absent. 3) If whitespace-only: 12. 4) Otherwise parse with lib/robots.mjs and evaluate all 126 names from references/ai-bots.json at '/'. 5) Compute round(allowed/126*12), minus 2 if any allowed bot's effective crawl-delay > 5.

parity.note: Full parity for a static robots.txt, except the RFC 9309 fixes listed in divergences. Differences: host-generated or CDN-managed robots.txt (Cloudflare managed robots.txt, rewrites, WordPress virtual robots.txt) is invisible in source; generated robots.txt is reported inconclusive; the site is evaluated at '/' only, so Disallow rules that target specific page paths are not scored.

fix_summary: Create or edit robots.txt so AI crawlers are allowed (e.g. remove 'Disallow: /' under AI bot groups, avoid Crawl-delay > 5), or add an empty/permissive 'User-agent: *\nAllow: /' file. Place it at public/robots.txt (Vite, Next.js, Astro), static/robots.txt (Hugo), a passthrough file (Eleventy) or site root (static HTML); for Next.js app/robots.ts edit the rules array. Write one User-agent line per group to avoid the extension's grouping bug.

divergences.extension: Consecutive User-agent lines: rules attach only to the last agent, earlier agents count as allowed.
divergences.plugin: Consecutive User-agent lines form one group that shares the rules (lib/robots.mjs).
divergences.reason: RFC 9309; the extension undercounted blocked bots in grouped records.

divergences.extension: Bot names match robots.txt tokens case-sensitively ('gptbot' does not match 'GPTBot').
Any matching Allow beats any matching Disallow.
divergences.plugin: Longest matching rule wins, Allow wins ties.
divergences.reason: RFC 9309 and Google behaviour; 'Allow: /blog' no longer unblocks '/'.

divergences.extension: The * group's Crawl-delay applies to bots that have their own group.
divergences.plugin: Only the Crawl-delay of the groups that apply to the bot counts.
divergences.reason: A bot with its own group ignores the * group.

divergences.extension: Inline comments ('Disallow: /x # note') become part of the pattern.
Status is explicit: pass only if every bot is allowed and no delay warning; warning if allowed > blocked.
divergences.plugin: Status is derived from the integer score by the shared 80% / 50% rule (e.g. 2 of 126 blocked still rounds to 12 and passes, with findings).

divergences.extension: Evaluates the current page's URL path; robots.txt fetched live (403/503 treated as missing).
divergences.plugin: Site check at '/', robots.txt read from the served root; a generated robots.txt is inconclusive instead of absent.
divergences.reason: Source vs live: the repo has no request path, and a generator's output cannot be read without building.

divergences.extension: All 126 bots count equally: score = round(allowed / 126 * 12), so blocking GPTBot and ClaudeBot still scores 12/12.
divergences.plugin: Ten major AI search and assistant crawlers (GPTBot, OAI-SearchBot, ChatGPT-User, ClaudeBot, Claude-SearchBot, Claude-User, PerplexityBot, Perplexity-User, Google-Extended, Applebot-Extended) share 9 points and the other 116 share 3: score = round(9 * majorAllowed / 10 + 3 * otherAllowed / 116). Blocking any major bot caps the score at 9 (a warning). The list lives in references/ai-bots.json (major_bots).
divergences.reason: Blocking the crawlers behind ChatGPT, Claude, Perplexity, Gemini and Apple Intelligence is what actually removes a site from AI answers; an obscure scraper should not weigh the same.

divergences.extension: Fetches /robots.txt live; an unreachable robots.txt is treated like a missing one.
divergences.plugin: URL mode (audit of a live URL): parses the fetched /robots.txt. A 404, another non-2xx status or an HTML fallback is absent (8/12). An unreachable answer (status 0, 401, 403, 429, 503, timeout or network error) is inconclusive at half weight (6/12). The robots.txt generator lookup in the repo is skipped. Results are measured, not predicted.
divergences.reason: Unreachable-vs-absent rule in the project CLAUDE.md; URL mode measures instead of predicting.
